So please continue with the cross-examination and give further thought to what you want to do with any other documents which may give rise to the re-opening of your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavranic, we have heard Witness Abdylhaqim Shaqiri here in this courtroom. He was the Prosecution witness who testified here on pages 2776 of the transcript and 2777. The said person stated that there was no KLA presence in the sector of Anamorava which is Vitina, Gnjilane, Kamenica, and other municipalities. Is this true what he claimed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. There were members of the KLA in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a military document which is P1310 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 5D1310.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see this document, please, item 11 from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And there it says that in the Pristina-Podujevo-Medvedja-Kosovska Kamenica-Gnjilane territory there is a large number of armed terrorists. It says that the majority of terrorists is in the area between Gnjilane and Presevo in the Uglare-Mucibaba-Predgrade triangle and that in the town of Gnjilane they are in settlements Gavran 1 and 2, Bela Zemlja, Sant Agin, Kamnik and that in that area there are about 2.000 of them armed, and counting civilians, that figure is double. This information dates from the 13th of April, 1999. Did you have similar data concerning terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did have similar data, perhaps even greater figures, not Uglajare, Mucibaba, Predgrade but Podgradje. Podgradje is the name of the place, that's the penultimate paragraph. I already spoke about the 7th operations on two brigades, 171st and 172nd. According to our information there was a large number of terrorists who later poured in from Pristina and Urosevac area to the area of Zlasevac and Marica and Zegovac and Zegovacka Vrbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In your testimony you spoke about the deployment of military forces. Would I be right in saying that the majority of the forces was deployed in the border area towards the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you have information to the effect that in the Republic of Macedonia there were very strong NATO forces there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had such information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this leading to something new, because if this is simply repetition of material we've already heard, Mr. Cepic, it's not really a reasonable use of cross-examination in your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just have one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gavranic, Vitina fell under the jurisdiction of the Gnjilane SUP, Vitina municipality?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's quite a large territory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Vitina there was the department of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But it's a large area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it is the area that is most densely populated within the Gnjilane SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were people moving out from the territory of Vitina?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my earlier evidence I said, and I will now repeat it and add a few things. The greatest numbers of people moving out were from the territory of the town of Gnjilane and the vicinity from Mucibaba and the area above Zegra towards the Macedonian border. As for the Kamenica portion which was covered by the Kamenica department of the interior and Vitinice territory covered by the Vitina department, not so many people were moving out. As far as I remember in Vitina there were just a few villages that were deserted, which percentage-wise was much lower than the other areas that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Gavranic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Gavranic, you will now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gavranic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I start by asking you briefly about your testimony that the MUP staff in Pristina was not an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior. By "organizational unit," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organizational unit is a term used in the original official documents of the Serbian MUP. It says there that organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior, there are two sectors, and then secretariats of the interior administrations are in turn organizational units of those sectors. Further on, in the rules it is stated which organizational units do not fall within sectors and I did not see in a single document that a staff was an organizational unit, which is an entity whose tasks and duties are very strictly defined by regulations and internal regulations of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Wasn't the minister of the interior and the -- or weren't the minister of the interior and the department heads empowered under the law to establish ad hoc units of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister did have power to do that, but department heads, if the translation I received was correct, did not have power. I don't know whether you perhaps had in mind heads of SUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When I said department heads I meant the heads of the state security section or department and the head of the public service department. Let's look at P1251 to see if we could get somewhere on this. This is a decision on the formation of the ministry staff.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it is signed by the assistant minister and department chief, General Djordjevic. I represent that to you. That is on the next page of the document. And it tells the -- tells exactly what the responsibilities of the staff is. If you look at paragraph 2 it says: "The task of the staff is to plan, organize, guide, and coordinate the work of the secretariats of the interior at the border police station on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in performing complex and important duties and assignments that involve ..." And it goes on to list various areas that the MUP staff was responsible to plan and coordinate. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you see that it starts by indicating that this is done pursuant to Article 10 of the book of rules of the internal organization of the Ministry of Interior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a mistranslation when it says "international"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's a mistranslation. Can you read the top --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it's I think quite clearly a mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you read the beginning of that statement, Mr. Gavranic where the reference to Article 10 appears.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Pursuant to Article 10 of the Book of Rules on internal organization of the Ministry of Interior."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's sufficient. Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we look at P1072, which is the Book of Rules of the internal organization, page 11 thereof where we'll find Article 10. And I think it's the same page in B/C/S, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it provides that the chief of the department may establish permanent or ad hoc staffs, commissions, task forces and working groups made up of ministry employees. So --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- having seen that, would you now agree with me that the ministry staff was an ad hoc administrative unit formed under the powers that were granted to the head of the department?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff of the ministry is an auxiliary organ of the ministry, as I have stated, established by the minister or chief of the sector could have done it pursuant to an authorisation of the minister. And as far as I know, he signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could look at P1505 quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not following you, Mr. Gavranic. What do you mean -- you raised -- you used this language yesterday, an auxiliary organ. What's the significance of the expression "auxiliary"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you asked me yesterday and I gave you an answer. I will describe to you how I perceived it as chief of SUP, the role of the staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, you've done that already. What Mr. Stamp is pointing out to you is that it's not something exceptional, that the rules provide clearly for the establishment of a staff with tasks. And you insist on describing that as an auxiliary organ of the ministry. Where do we find the idea that this is somehow auxiliary, isn't part of the ministry itself? The rules seem to suggest that it is part of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you asked me how I saw it as chief of SUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand all that. All he's asking you is whether it doesn't look from the document that you're now having your attention drawn to that it's a perfectly legitimate step for the head of the service to appoint a staff to carry out tasks of the ministry. Do you not agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do agree with that. It's regulated in Article 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the minister could legitimately appoint or create a group like the ministry staff which would have responsibility for the management of the SUPs in some areas of their activity, for example, anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister could do a lot of things. I don't know what were all the things that the minister could do. The minister could do a great many things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, if we look at P1505, which is before you, this is the minister establishing the staff on the 16th of June, 1998. He does so by ordering that the decision which I showed you, that is the decision of the head of the department, and this is at paragraph 6, you may not be able to see, but at paragraph 6 he orders that General Djordjevic's decision shall come into force, that is an earlier decision establishing the staff. And he does so pursuant to his powers under, among other things, Article 7 of the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say to you is that this decision is from 1998, and at that time I was chief of SUP in Zrenjanin. As for this communication through these decisions, I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Article 7 is on the first page I think, the section invoking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Paragraph 6 of this revokes the Djordjevic order; it doesn't bring it into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My translation of paragraph 6 reads that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that this document is not on the list that we got from the Prosecution for this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem you have is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not on our list either, and it was on the list of Mr. Lazarevic but it wasn't used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there's a good chance that I will be using it, and I think in these circumstances and bearing in mind the questions that the Bench asked of the last witness relating to this document, then I think on this occasion it is appropriate to follow up on this. And we've also got an issue which I hope you may be the one to resolve which is the translation of paragraph 6. Does it say: "... The following shall come into force or out of force ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps we could ask the witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, Mr. Gavranic, could you read paragraph 6, that might be the best way to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph number 6: "With this decision coming into force, the following shall come out of force: Decision to establish ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's sufficient. That's the translation that we have, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Actually, I asked for another translation and got a different translation. I'll have to go by the one we just have on the record now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But this makes sense, doesn't it -- well, maybe not. Otherwise you would have two staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily, but I think the translation that we have now is the one that we have to live with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The point, however, Mr. Gavranic, is that the minister was empowered and did set up this staff pursuant to his powers under the Law on Internal Affairs. Now, what I want to ask you -- and I wish to show you that, the Law on Internal Affairs, which is P1737. Section 6 deals with the organizational units of the ministry and section 7, which is under the same general rubric, organizational units, provides that the minister -- is the document coming up?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that, what you are talking about right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your patience will be rewarded. There we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Article 6 deals with the organizational units in general. Article 7, which is a provision under which the minister created the staff provides that: "The minister shall determine the manner in which the Ministry of the Interior performs its duties and issue instructions for its performance."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already given my comments on that in relation to the dispatches that we looked at, what the priority tasks of the SUPs are in that period. I can only talk about that part in relation to the SUPs and to my own SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but I wonder if in seeing these provisions you will agree with me that the minister in the regular discharge of his duties could establish a staff that had responsibility to manage the activities of the SUPs in the -- and in their anti-terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are now talking to me about two things. You are saying that the minister can establish a staff on the territory of several SUPs and also in relation to anti-terrorist activities. The SUP, the secretariat of the interior, I've already explained that throughout my testimony, I explained what all the work it does is. Secretariats in wartime do the same work they did in peacetime except under more complex conditions. Anti-terrorist work is not carried out by secretariats of the interior, it's not carried out by SUPs. The SUP is not engaged in anti-terrorist combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. But what I want you to comment on is whether or not you will agree with me that the MUP staff was regularly established by the minister to exercise responsibilities that included management of some of the activities of the SUPs.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand what it is that you're trying to get from me by way of a resolution to this problem. The staff of the MUP was founded in Pristina and you showed me the document on the basis of what it was established. And I said what the purpose of this staff was in terms of the personal experience I have. I did not have any other documents in relation to that that would prescribe what it was that this staff did and what my duties as chief of SUP were vis-a-vis the staff. I worked on the basis of the documents I received from the heads of the administrations at the ministry headquarters in Belgrade. I've already explained the ad hoc work which the MUP staff did in Kosovo and Metohija by way of assisting the SUPs there. I can only talk from the point of view of the chief of the secretariat of the interior. As for the relationship between the minister and his auxiliary organs on the basis of Article 10, that he established on the basis of Article 10, is something that I cannot talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem with that approach, Mr. Gavranic, is that you're a member of this body that was set up under the document P1505 because the expanded staff is to include the chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I never -- I was never a member of the staff nor did anyone ever inform me that I was a member of the staff. When I went to meetings in Pristina that was held up until the war, these were the meetings of the collegium of the ministry. When I went there, when I was sent there, nobody ever told me that I was a member of the MUP staff, I as chief of the SUP in Gnjilane, that I was a member of the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I had intended to ask you about that. You said that these were meetings of the collegium. What do you mean by collegium in these circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain. As chiefs of SUP we would go and attend regular meetings at the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade, meetings with the minister or the head of section that we called collegiums. Sometimes it would be meetings of all the head chiefs, sometimes only of some SUPs. So when I came to Gnjilane, I continued to function in the same way, go to the collegiums in Pristina where the minister would come or the head of the section, and sometimes these collegium meetings of the chiefs of SUP were held even without them, and that is how I understood these meetings and how all of us understood these meetings. May I just add one more thing to that in terms of these collegiums? We prepared some information related to the state of security in the areas covered by our respective SUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let us look at the minutes of one of those meetings. Can we look at P1989. This is a record of a meeting of the senior police officers in Kosovo and Metohija on the 4th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And just so that we could get the translation right since we are having problems with the translation, could you just read the first sentence of the second paragraph. I think it says: "The meeting was held by ..."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The meeting was held by Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic and Major-General Sreten Lukic and was attended by the chiefs of all secretariats, PJP detachment commanders, the SAJ commander, and the RDB JSO commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think you were shown, and this is at page 2 in the English and also the same page in the B/C/S, that you yourself, you reported, among other things, on persons who had been arrested in your area, persons who had moved out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, that document indicates that the JSO commander from the RDB was present, it refers in a number of places to terrorism, and it's essentially a meeting that you describe as a collegium and you say terrorism has got nothing to do with you. Now, how do you account for that being the subject discussed in this minute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain this in the following way. The chiefs of SUPs reported about the subject matter pertaining to the functioning of the secretariat of the interior, and the commanders of the PJP detachments, the JSO, and the SAJ who were in charge of combatting terrorism and that is an area that cannot be outside the SUP. So within Kosovo and Metohija they reported about those tasks and assignments for which they were established and for which they existed. So these are two different things, they are two different groups. We reported about all the things that the SUP deals with, not to repeat all that, crime, public law and order, and so on and so forth, and commanders of the detachments of the PJP, the commander of the SAJ, and the commander of the JSO are trained for anti-terrorist activity. And their basic tasks involve the struggle against terrorism. That is what I was trying to say a few minutes ago. It is not the SUP that is in charge of that struggle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you look at the Pec secretariat chief's comments, you'll see that he talks of: "Control of the territory has been established, anti-terrorist operations will ensue in the areas of Istok and Rugovo (it is estimated that there are 350 terrorists)." So why is he reporting on that if it's not his responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to explain this to you in the following way, Your Honour. He, as the chief of SUP, has to know whether the patrols can go to all areas covered by his secretariat, whether it is safe, whether there were terrorist attacks against them, whether there were some problems in relation to that. Also, the chief of SUP, when he cross-references the intelligence he has and the operative information he has from this area covered by security, he has to know whether there are terrorists in that area or not, whether it is dangerous or not dangerous, and so on. So all of this information we had from the ground were yet another contribution to a better awareness of the situation as it was in the field. The chiefs of SUP had to know what was happening and they had to control the territory according to sectors. Every sector has its leader and they have to report about the state of safety and security. If they say civilians complain to patrols that it is not safe in a particular area, there are attacks against patrols, that means that there is in effect no control over that territory. So they gave their own assessments. Now, I don't know to what extent they were taken into account because these evaluations or assessments were received from different security structures, but we gave our own opinions on what the situation was in terms of security there in the area of our respective SUPs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at page 2 of the same document, you will see that you yourself, you are reporting about terrorist groups being crushed and parts of groups are being inserted in the Zegovac sector. So again you see here you are not only reporting on the presence of terrorist groups, but action taken in respect of the terrorist groups. Why would this be your responsibility, especially when as we can see on this page the members of the PJP detachments or the leaders of the PJP detachments are present? And it would be their responsibility, if I understand you correctly, to do that sort of reporting.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This second paragraph, I mean my report was as follows. Terrorist gangs from the area of Pristina are infiltrating the area of Zegovac, and my report had to do with the fact that this territory was under jeopardy and that I could not control it because terrorist gangs from the area of Pristina are moving to the area of Zegovac, and later on I think an action, an anti-terrorist action would follow, a joint one between the army and the police, in that area. That is to say that the SUP cannot report on the breaking of the terrorist gangs because I could not and did not carry out anti-terrorist actions in the territory of my SUP. Not a single chief did that. That was done by the PJPs, members of special police units, they did that in accordance with their own plans. So the point of this was that terrorist gangs should be broken up. Zegovac is to the south of Pristina, and on the left, on the west, it borders Urosevac. Terrorist gangs showed up there and the police did not dare go there any longer and they could not keep this area under their own control because police vehicles were fired at. I was warning about that, that in that area there were terrorists. And everyone knows who is supposed to fight terrorists. We as the SUP are not trained and equipped for anti-terrorist struggle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We'll get back to the role of the SUP a little later, but since we're on this document, if you look at page 3 and you see item 2 there.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What does that say?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following tasks: "Sreten Lukic MUP carries out all tasks like in peacetime and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask for the text to be adjusted, it was read out very fast. It's towards the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment--

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I read on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- Mr. Stamp, we don't have the text and it's difficult to follow. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I just want you to read the first two lines at paragraph 2. Could you --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I? "Forthcoming tasks. "Sreten Lukic, head of the staff of the ministry" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you will see that he goes on to issue one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten tasks. Under what authority did Sreten Lukic as head of the staff issue instructions and tasks to the heads of the MUPs and the heads of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Sreten Lukic warned us here practically that we should step up all the things that we were doing anyway. If you look at the second bullet point, the MUP in time of war, just like in peacetime, does everything it is supposed to do; that is to say that as far as perpetrators of crimes are concerned, the attitude is the same. Quite simply, he instructs us to act as expeditiously and as efficiently as possible in carrying out our regular work, of course in a situation that is more difficult. I really don't know now --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I mean I just focus --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- what it is that you -- what I was supposed to explain to you in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just focus on the question I asked you, and if you look at those tasks, some of them are quite specific instructions. The question is this: Under what authority does Sreten Lukic, as head of the staff of the ministry in Pristina, issue tasks to SUP chiefs, PJP commanders, JSO chiefs, what authority? That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know on the basis of what, but he did not issue any special tasks to us that were not in accordance with the tasks that we were already involved in according to our own plan of work. So there is nothing new there, nothing that we hadn't already been doing in the first place, I'm talking about the SUP, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, this is rather different from what you indicated yesterday was the purpose of the staff and that you wanted to repeat earlier today. You told us about this auxiliary body that would give you assistance. Now we see the head of the staff doing something quite different from that, and that's what Mr. Stamp is looking for an explanation for. How does he fit in, where does he fit in, giving this type of instruction about use of ammunition, the use of radio communication, clearing up the battle-field, dealing with paramilitary units, and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said already what the SUP expected from the staff, and what we received from the staff were different reports, too, cumulative ones about the state of security generally speaking. It was their analysis man who worked on that. And very often we got dispatches and information of different kinds from them when we were cautioned that we should work as SUPs do, equally, in terms of crime prosecution. I already explained that we were being urged to have some things carried out, or rather, I would ask them to make an effort on our behalf. That was one way. Also, very often from the staff we got different reports, analytical reports, how our colleagues acted in different secretariats and how we should act. And so we could follow the situation cumulatively in that way and we could all take equal measures and work efficiently. I got a multitude of dispatches from the staff via courier, involving tasks in relation to how to treat civilians, the population that is outside urban areas, that is a different kind of communication. I got that from the staff. So it's on the basis of that that we acted, on the basis of that. But the SUPs don't really have anything to do with anti-terrorist actions or did the staff send anything to us about that or did they issue any tasks to us about that. I never received anything from the staff along those lines. Because probably when we sent reports on the basis of these instructions and information, you could see that we acted differently as chiefs of SUPs. Some had crimes, others did not. Some had many crimes of one particular kind, others of a different kind. After analysing these dispatches, the SUP warned about this and asked for equal processing. That was the line: The staff-the SUPs, the SUPs-the staff, and that is how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to this document, but having regard to your answer now can we look at P1996, a document that you have been shown by counsel. This is the minutes of the meeting held in the MUP staff for Kosovo on the 7th of May, 1999. If you look at page 10 in the English, and I'll remind you that you were present at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At page 10 of the English we see where it indicates that the head of the staff gave it to assistant minister Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic, and if we go to page 11 in the English which is page 9 in the B/C/S, we see what General Obradovic [sic] told you and we see item 2. To ensure that there's no issue in respect to the translation, can you read item 2 of the instructions the assistant minister Obradovic [sic] gave you. Read it aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant minister Obrad Stevanovic under 2: "Anti-terrorist actions. In some areas they progressed slowly, encountered major problems. After the end of some of the larger actions, such as the 'Budakovo-Jezerce' one, each SUP will be expected to work independently on organizing anti-terrorist actions in their own areas. The plan must be approved by the staff" -- I apologise. "The plan must be approved by the staff and will be carried out with manoeuvre detachments." May I explain this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but what I want you to explain is your evidence given to us now and yesterday that the SUPs were not involved in anti-terrorist activity, and here you have the minister precisely and expressly telling you that you should be involved. And secondly, when you said that the role of the staff was to supplement your supplies, for example, with passports and they were merely auxiliary, when we see here that the plan -- your anti-terrorist plans had to be approved by the staff. Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is taking place in May. I read the second paragraph. The second sentence reads as follows: "After the end of some of the larger actions, such as the 'Budakovo-Jezerce' one, each SUP will be expected to work independently on organizing anti-terrorist actions in their own areas." What does this mean? If there are any terrorists in the territory of the Gnjilane SUP--I will try to be specific by giving you a specific example-- if there were terrorists and they were controlling a certain territory and if the reports were received that they were active in some areas, then, since every SUP had its own company, the PJP company, the plan for such activities was drawn up by the commander of the company, and this commander would take this to his detachment commander. In the Gnjilane SUP example, that was the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade, and they agreed on how to carry out this anti-terrorist action. So what was my task, me as the chief of SUP in that area, and the task of the SUP in general in that area? I had to know when this action was to be carried out in order to take all measures necessary so that patrols would not go on their routine duty in that area. I had to prepare hospitals to accept any injured or wounded persons. Also, we had to ensure accommodation for people withdrawing from the area due to anti-terrorist activities and so on. So people from the SUP had to know what was going on in the area. Chiefs of SUP had to know what was going on, otherwise there would have been chaos because if an anti-terrorist unit in the form of a company or several companies or in the form of a detachment, if they were active in their area, I as chief of SUP had to know about this, otherwise I would have carried on with my routine daily work without knowing what was happening in my area, and my routine work was crime prevention and so on, combatting crime and so on. And I had to prepare the entire logistics in connection with the consequences of these anti-terrorist activities. Any reported murders, if there were any… The wounded had to be taken care of. We had to ensure that there were people constantly on duty in hospitals and so on. That was the role of the SUP and that was the plan that I had to have if such an anti- terrorist activity was announced to me through my company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Wrongly translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which are you referring?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In line -- 66 page, line 12: "And I had to prepare the entire logistics for these anti-terrorist activities." The witness didn't say that. He mentioned aftermaths of these anti-terrorist activities, but it can be heard if you listen to the tape, but we can clarify it with this witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I think that's one where I'll invite CLSS to translate that sentence again. That's page 66, lines 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Gnjilane SUP had how many PJP brigades or units attached to it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a single brigade in the Gnjilane SUP. There were no units resubordinated to the Gnjilane SUP. In the Gnjilane SUP we had a PJP company numbering about 120 people, and when they were not on a mission within their brigade they were carrying out routine activities just like all other policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they were not engaged in anti-terrorist activities, they carried out routine, regular tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The company in the Gnjilane SUP, they were also associated with the PJP brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. They were part of the 124th Intervention Brigade for Kosovo and Metohija. This brigade had several companies and they were just a part of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when the company prepared anti-terrorist plans or plans for anti-terrorist actions, wouldn't you as SUP commander see these plans?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, I'm not a SUP commander. I don't know if I received good interpretation. I'm chief of SUP. The chief of SUP didn't see these plans, nor did he approve them. These brigades [as interpreted] were drawn up at the level of a brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, briefly, it went away from our screens, but since you wanted CLSS to check this I think it needs to be expanded from page 65, line 13, to page 66, line 13. I think that there is several mistakes in the transcript and I would like them to listen to the entire page. At 66, line 10, line 11, and so on I see -- perhaps it should be checked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it all on page 66 because it --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I guess this happened, somebody made a mistake in interpretation because of the speed, and if they listen over to the tape perhaps they could correct it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My question is whether all the problems are on page 66 because that's half the translation or other mistakes you say possibly on page 65 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I see are mistakes on page 66, but since it was going quite fast and it's obvious that the mistakes were due to the speed and not to some other reason, perhaps it would be a good reason to check the entire answer of this witness. It would be good to check the entire answer. It's just additional ten lines, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For the avoidance of doubt, then we will agree to your request. That's from 65, 13, to 66, 13. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that I mentioned line 12 before so it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Of what page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So line 12 should be included as well, 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, line 12 comes before 13, Mr. Lukic, so you should be okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, my mistake. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I know that you're saying now that as chief of the SUP Gnjilane you were concerned about your regular duties and the PJPs would be involved in the anti-terrorist activity. And I think you are saying that you had to make provisions, for example, to ensure that there would be no patrols going into the area where anti-terrorist activity would take place. In those circumstances, am I to understand that you would not see the plan for anti-terrorist activity at all?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We obviously misunderstood each other. The patrols did not go to those areas when anti-terrorist activities were undertaken there. This was probably another mistranslation. I told them that the patrols did not go there. If we had an assessment that there were terrorists there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's exactly what Mr. Stamp put to you, that you would have to make sure that there was no -- there were no patrols in the areas where the action was to be undertaken. And he's asking you how you can do that if you don't see the plans.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will explain this to you simply. So if an assessment was made that in the territory of a particular SUP there were terrorists, then those assessments were made public, or rather, I would give those assessments to my company commander. If you saw the minutes where I was recorded as saying that there were problems in the territory of Zegovac, if this was a small-scale anti-terrorist action, then a commander would go see his brigade commander, they would draw a plan together, and I would only be informed about the area where this was to be conducted. I was not informed about how this was going to be conducted. So I would be expecting consequences and I would inform public utility companies, hospitals, and so on, I would inform the people that there would be an anti-terrorist action, and this action would be planned without the SUP involvement. Nobody informed me about this, this was not something that was routinely done. PJP would go, my company commander would inform me so that I wouldn't plan the people for regular, routine tasks, and the people would go out. Chiefs of SUP knew nothing about their future, or rather, further engagement. So the company commander would inform me. It just so happened that my company commander was also head of the police department, and he would inform me that he was expected to show up at the brigade command, which would mean that for the following day or two I was not to plan these people for routine activities in fighting crime, in keeping law and order, and so on, because 120 policemen were leaving my area to go on a different mission. What they were to do, where they were to do that, is something that chiefs of SUP were not informed about. These are two different things. I hope I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But again, I don't want to belabour the point. What you just said when asked is that where they were to go, you were not informed about that. How could you not be informed about where they were to go or where the action was to take place if you had to make provisions to ensure that no patrols would be present or you had to advise public utilities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to ensure that we understood each other. When I said where they were going, if they were going outside of the jurisdiction of the particular SUP, if the company received summons to report to the brigade command in Pristina, naturally I knew in which area there would be activity when it came to my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The assistant minister Stevanovic also instructed that the anti-terrorist plans were to be approved by the staff. Were you aware that the staff had responsibility to approve these plans?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that. I wasn't aware of that. What I as chief of SUP knew about came to the level of the brigade command. So members of my secretariat would report to their intervention brigade. I think that Zarko Brakovic was commander of that intervention brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we continue with this document, at the bottom of page 11 in English, and I think you need to go to the top of page 10 in B/C/S, you see that assistant minister Stevanovic said: "The commanders of the A and B detachments are subordinated to the chief of SUP and must attend staff meetings." What's the A and B detachments? Are these PJP detachments?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each SUP had an A detachment, which was a manoeuvre unit, a PJP company, and they had a B unit, which was a territorial company covering a certain territory once anti-terrorist activities are over. I did not have PJP detachments, but it is also not true that they were subordinated to the chief of SUP. That's not true, nor were they ever subordinated to him. I can give you an interpretation of this, based on discussions with my colleagues who had detachments. So commanders of detachment who were stationed in the territory of a certain SUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How does that fit with your own area where you only had one company of PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that in Kosovo everybody had just one PJP company. I had half a company, if I may say so, two territorial platoons together with Urosevac. And they were guarding the location near Crnoljevo, which is on Stimlje-Prizren road, people guarded that road. And I saw them -- I found them there when I came, they were there throughout in 1998 and 1999. So this B formation was practically in that territory. It wasn't equipped for anti-terrorist activities. They simply provided security on the Stimlje-Prizren road. And since in the Urosevac SUP they had some problems with the strength, this is how we achieved it. As I said, I found them there when I came and they throughout assisted me in regular duties and tasks because we had huge problems, and that was throughout the war and in 1998, as I told you, I found them there in 1998 and then they were there in 1999 and this B formation went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, it will help us if you try to confine your answers to the particular question. I'm -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you had one company, but now you tell us you had half a company. And then you tell us something about working on a particular road. It's not helping me understand the set-up, especially since, as I understand it, this meeting was in May and the minister is recorded as saying: "The commanders of the A and B detachments are subordinated to the chief of SUP and must attend staff meetings." Now, you can understand our difficulties when we see these two very plain statements, and you certainly would appear to be contradicting the first of these and then going on to tell us that none of the PJP companies were big enough to provide two detachments for any SUP chief in Kosovo. But the meeting's only to do with Kosovo, so it's an utterly confusing situation as far as I can see. Now, can you briefly shed any light on this? Please don't try to go over what you've said already. Is there something you can say in simple language to clarify this for us, why this would be said and be so contradictory apparently to the things you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will attempt to be clear. Each SUP, even when I was in Zrenjanin, had an A and B unit within their PJPs. They had two companies, A and B. The same applied in Kosovo when I went to Gnjilane, there was an A formation, A company, of the PJP which was a manoeuvre unit which took part in actions; and then there was the B company, which was not independent but constituted one company together with the people from the Urosevac SUP. So there was a joint company of the Gnjilane SUP and Urosevac SUP. That was the B company. So the A formation is a manoeuvre one, it goes into actions, it is equipped for anti-terrorist activities. The B company is not a manoeuvre company, it is a territorial unit, and it is engaged when there are anti-terrorist activities in order to secure the territory where anti-terrorist activities had already been conducted. I don't know if I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So your SUP had two detachments, A and B, and were these detachments composed of companies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not understand each other again. We had two companies, A and B. A detachment is something else. So we had an A company, which was a manoeuvre one, and a B company that we shared with the Urosevac SUP. A detachment is something larger and there were none in the territory of the Gnjilane SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we have the witness read that passage. You said it's on page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the first full paragraph of page 10 in B/C/S, could you read the last sentence thereof, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Commanders of A and B formations detachments are subordinated to the chief of SUP and they must attend collegiums." No, commanders of PJPs are not subordinated to SUP chiefs. How this came to be included in this document, what this meant, I don't know because I did not have detachments. But I do know that they were not subordinated to the SUP chief when they were on a mission within their PJPs or detachments. Commander of a company was subordinated to me only when on routine tasks, when he went into his unit, he was not subordinated to me. So it is my position that chief of SUPs are something quite different from detachment commanders. There is no hierarchy relationship of subordination between them. These are two completely different entities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have your explanation of that or your answer at least. Mr. Lukic, earlier in the case I think we had evidence that a detachment is bigger than a brigade, never --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Detachment is approximately 400, 500 people; brigade is 5.000 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Right. Okay. So detachment --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But this brigade, police brigade, is different from military brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. I understand that. But you're saying the evidence so far is that the detachment is something smaller than a brigade in the police; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me check that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, detachment is 500 people, brigade in -- police brigade, 800 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Right. The word that's used here for A and B was translated in two ways by the interpreter, formation and detachment were the two English words used. Is the word in Serb the same word as is used for the detachment that normally has 500 people in it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So there may be confusion caused in this minute by the Serb language, never mind the translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But both A and B are detachments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the witness is saying clearly that a place -- a SUP like Gnjilane or any other SUP in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Companies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- would not have detachments, it would have a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we know a company -- he gave us a figure for the numbers in a company, which is much smaller than a detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A company is 120 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is included in SUP and there are eight companies in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the word -- yeah. But the word used here is not company. The word used here is detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Detachment is not part of SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that, but the same word is used here for detachment. It's the word for detachment that's used in relation to A and B, and that doesn't make any sense bearing in mind that individual SUPs do not have detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the document we can see detachment, you are right, in original, in Serbian version also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All I'm wanting to be clear about at the moment from you, because neither of us should be giving evidence, is that the confusion here may stem from bad use of or careless use of the Serb language.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Might be, but also I don't think that this witness is good to -- good one to explain detachments because he didn't have any in his area. He didn't have sent detachments from the Serbia in his area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He didn't have a single one. He -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You may feel you've explored it enough, you may feel you want to explore it more, Mr. Stamp. I'm inclined to think we've heard as much as is going to be useful on this particular topic from this witness and might be best to resume on something else after lunchtime. Mr. Gavranic, we now need to break for lunch for approximately an hour. Would you again leave the courtroom with the usher and we will resume at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you've asked us with your client's consent to agree to the examination of the next witness, Lekoski, being conducted by Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are prepared in the circumstances to allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We would appreciate more notice in future of such applications which were -- this one was brought to our attention only this morning in the course of the sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We were looking at P1996 and if we could turn over to the next page in English which was the last page, page 12, and this is page 10 of the B/C/S. You will see there in his closing speech, head of the staff Major-General Lukic said, and there is one point, and the second point that General Lukic mentions is, I quote: "I especially mention that in the work of the OPG, the chief of SUP gives his permission for certain actions and informs the head of staff about them." What were the OPGs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are operative pursuit groups consisting of ten men each. In the Gnjilane SUP there were ten of them. These were the best-trained men and they were from the company I mentioned, and they belonged to the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So the head of the staff is telling you that you should give permission for certain actions of these groups. What did you understand General Lukic to be authorising you to do?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the following way. If there was a regular action, for example, in the Gavran neighbourhood in Gnjilane in wartime we had operative information that there were terrorists there, that there were weapons there, that there were terrorists or ammunition or something similar. I would inform my company commander. Such a risky and dangerous operation cannot be carried out by ordinary policemen; it has to be carried out by the best-trained policemen. That's why I needed the agreement -- agreement for that. So the company commander would inform the brigade commander and he would say that the chief of the SUP was asking for an OPG, an operative pursuit group, to be engaged to search a part of the neighbourhood or a building in the Gavran neighbourhood. That's what it referred to. As we had operative knowledge from the ground, from the sector, we would do that and these were risky tasks that could not be done by untrained policemen engaged in everyday tasks. It would have to the PJP, but if we were searching a building we would need somebody even better equipped and that would be the OPG. They were the best equipped and the best trained for such tasks. But in order to do that, I would need the agreement of their commander and they were part of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But could you explain to me what does he mean when he says that you give your permission. What do you give your permission to -- well, it says you give your permission to certain actions. As chief of the SUP, weren't you authorised by General Lukic to give your permission for certain actions of these OPGs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you can see that I am informing the staff leader or manager, and of course I would have to plan this action. I had the necessary information, but I didn't have approval. I have to make the assessment based on information coming from the ground from my colleagues. So, for example, I decide that it's necessary to search a building or to arrest someone, and this was wartime. I've already said how difficult and dangerous it was to arrest people. They were armed --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a minute. I think we are sort of losing the focus because you said that you would plan the action. How? How would you -- well, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, firstly, did you say you would plan the action in the employment of these OPGs, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would plan to conduct a search of a building, but I would not be able to do it in the ordinary way with ordinary policemen as I would in a less-risky situation. For example, I would plan the arrest -- I would plan the fact that Zmajevic Vlado has to be arrested, but I couldn't do that with ordinary policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how would you inform General Lukic about this activity?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the way I described earlier, through urgent informing, urgent reports. That would be a significant event on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we move off this document if I may move on to something else in the document, you said that Mr. Sainovic made a political speech, but I think if we look at the document itself we see that he appeared to be aware with the details of police operations. For example, he says at one point: "After operation Jezerce, there will no longer being a large-scale terrorist stronghold except for 30" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, the witness did not hear the entire question, the entire question was not interpreted, that's why I'm afraid there might be a misunderstanding. Could the question be repeated and interpreted for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, can you repeat the essence of the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have here, for example, General -- sorry, Mr. Sainovic saying: "After operation Jezerce," and this is at page 2 of the English, I think you have the B/C/S in front of you, "there will no longer be a large terrorist strong-hold except for 30 to 40 smaller-scale strong-holds numbering 500 to 700 terrorists in the areas in which the secretariats themselves will destroy and completely neutralize." It might be subject to interpretation, but this is not exactly a political speech. Firstly, who -- how would Mr. Sainovic receive information of that nature?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I'm the right person to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You don't know that, if --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- excuse me. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Go on. You were ...

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said if I see a document dated the 7th of May -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document of the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That in essence there was the most politics in this, but as for other matters I don't know. I'm really not the right person, I'm really not competent to reply to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic spoke in relative detail about police operations in Kosovo, and all I want to know if you know who, if anybody, reported to Mr. Sainovic about these police operations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. If we could quickly have a look at another one of these meetings, P1990, and this is the MUP staff meetings for the 19th or the 17th of February, 1999. This is another one that you attended I think you said.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just let me take a look. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: A meeting attended by the minister, the assistant ministers, department chiefs, and we see that it was opened by General Lukic. And if we go on to page 2 in English, and that's the bottom of your page 1, we see that in his opening remarks General Lukic speaks about 4.000 policemen and -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The bottom of page 1 and --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you read that sentence aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The staff planned," is that the sentence you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To carry out when the order is given three actions of cleaning the terrain of terrorists in the area of Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica and has allotted around 4.000 policemen, around 70 policemen from the operative pursuit group, and around 900 reservists."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The language seems clear to me, but can you explain to me what was the role of the staff in this operation involving 4.000 policemen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here when the order is given. Who gives the order, I don't know, the chief of the SUP, I am the last person to know that. The staff planned to carry out when the order is given, three mopping-up operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But the role of the staff was to plan and prepare this operation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you, PJP -- I am not the right person to talk about detachments. The chief of the SUP, this has nothing to do with the PJP or the detachments when they are engaged with manoeuvre units, only when they are carrying out ordinary tasks and then they are outside the PJP and the detachments. And then you can ask me anything you like about what they do. But as for this, I'm really not familiar with what they were doing ask how.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you were at that meeting. Didn't you understand General Lukic to be saying that his MUP staff in Pristina was responsible for planning and carrying out this major operation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that meeting, I'm just reading what it says, that's how I understood it, the way it's written down. I didn't understand it in any other way. When the order is given, so somebody has to give an order for this to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not the right person to answer this. I don't know anything about detachments and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the next sentence here it says that: "On Saturday, 20th of February, 1999, a meeting of the staff will be held with all police unit detachments commanders for further consultations about their engagements. Meetings have been held with all the RPO and they were attended by General Momcilo Stojanovic and Lieutenant Blagoje Pesic." The RPOs were the village -- what were the RPOs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: RPOs were reserve police detachments. I found them there. They existed in 1998 also, and they were in the villages. Such reserve police squads, there were about ten of them -- or police stations, rather. And on my territory, the territory covered by the Gnjilane SUP, they simply fell apart because they were all reservists and they had wartime assignments. They were assigned to the reserves to the army, the military territorial detachments, civilian protection, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, these RPOs which you say were set up in 1998 or you went there and saw them, were they not set up by order of General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, General Momcilo Stojanovic was in charge of them and that's what it says here too. What I was told when I arrived in the area, and later on I was able to see how they worked and this was a time of great tension, they were used to defend the villages should there be an aggression. But this never actually happened because they simply fell apart. Through them we received certain operative information at SUP level concerning the security situation and so on. Momcilo Stojanovic and the Lieutenant-Colonel, I think was his rank, Blagoje Pesic were tasked with their organization and work and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These units fell under the aegis of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were not units, these were reserve police stations of five or six men, sometimes there were three or four. These were not units, they were reserve police departments or stations, branch stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there must have been a mistranslation. These reserve police, earlier I see where you were translated as saying they were reserve police detachments. They are reserve police stations, correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Reserve police departments or branch stations, these were small departments numbering five or six men, and they were part of police stations in the regular way of things. I had these in five or six villages, but this is something else. These were reserve police stations established in 1998, and they never numbered more than three, four, or five men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Causing a confusion a bit because it says several times branch stations. So I would like to explore this with the witness, otherwise I would be suggestive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're saying that this is an inaccurate translation, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He never mentioned this. In the system there are stations and branch stations but not -- this is not what he meant when explaining this formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The translation in the document, Mr. Lukic, is reserve police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Shouldn't be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, can you read -- I need to find it in the Serb as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is this P1990?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's P1990, Mr. Stamp, and there's a reference to RPOs --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and we need a proper translation of RPOs, I think. Must be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I had it as reserve police station in the document and I think in P1990 in the B/C/S I think it's the approximate middle of the first page or towards the end of the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic says it should not be translated as reserve police stations, so that's what we need to get clear. Can you get the witness to read a passage that includes reference to RPO. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, if you could look in the next-to-last paragraph of page 1 of that document, the 17th of February, 1999, document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that in the official CLSS database "odilenje milicija" is given as branch police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. It's odilenje milicija policija, but this is completely different. This is RPO, reserve police and that word that should be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's have it read, Mr. Stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you see where it speaks of RPOs in nearly all the villages inhabited by Serbs, could you read that out loud, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Meetings were held with reserve police outposts where General Momcilo Stojanovic and Blagoje Pesic were." Reserve police outposts have nothing to do with police stations. A police station is something else. And a police branch station is something else. This is a reserve police outpost.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, is it a place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, those are villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but are the reserve police based in a building in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they don't have premises, they don't have a building or a place to be in. They're there in case of aggression. They can be engaged. We have an officer maintaining liaison with them, and these are local men and there were three, four, or five of them in each village, both Serbs and Albanians. So this was something that was established in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I found it in Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, how would you translate the letter O and the word that it stands for?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It could be squad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, reserve police will do. Let's carry on, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These reserve police entities, were they not established and organized by order of General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they were established because they were there when I arrived --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's good enough. If you don't know, there's no point in speculating. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look quickly at P2804.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from General Lukic of the 10th of July, 1998, before you are in Kosovo. Unfortunately the B/C/S is not very clear --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could you please speak into the microphone, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is also not announced, but Your Honour should decide on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, the document was not on our original list. We had sent an e-mail recently, as soon as it came to my attention, that we would like to use this document. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why is this one important?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I think I can ask the question without the document, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, try to do that and let's see where we get to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One clarification, we received the e-mail with the number of another document, not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And -- very well. Never mind. I'm told that there was a correction subsequently, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Gavranic, weren't you shown documents when you took over your post indicating that these reserve police entities were organized by the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this document. It wasn't shown to me, but I did know in practice that there were these reserve police entities because several times General Momcilo Stojanovic came and I remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're -- you've --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've answered the question. In the circumstances, we will allow you to use the document, Mr. Stamp, since it may assist to clarify a measure of confusion about these squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document that perhaps I should ask you to read the second paragraph where it speaks of organizing the defence of villages, can you read that aloud, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Carry out plan of combat training in all reserve police entities, or squads, in accordance with the plan that was submitted to you." It's July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not what the current -- oh, it is in the second part. Is that the bit you wanted read?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You weren't interested in organizing the defence of the villages?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, the part I wanted read was just for the translation of RPO, but I don't know if there are any translation issues in respect to the first part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: They're obviously a group of personnel, and exactly what they're called is neither here nor there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many of these personnel did you find in Gnjilane SUP when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN GAVRANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that in about 20 villages that were there, to the best of my knowledge, they had such squads. They existed for a very short period of time, they fell apart when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's be clear about numbers. Earlier you said in about 10 villages I think. Was it 10 or 20?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
